From SWAK to Strength - the story of how Crestway High turned its fortunes around

By: Marion Edmunds | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We show how Crestway High, the school with the worst matric marks in 2024 in the Western Cape was able to turn itself around to get a dramatically improved pass rate the following year

Unique Selling Point:
We have unique access to a struggling school in Retreat, on the Cape Peninsula, which is on the edge of Cape Ganglands, and provides an academic home for about a thousand children from severely disadvantaged backgrounds, children who don't always have enough to eat, often live with family members as their parents do not take responsibility for them, and who have to manage a rough world of gangs and violence outside the school gates. Academic Prof Jonathan Jansen, having read about the plight of the school when they scored the worst in the province for their class of 2023 in January of 2024, decided to intervene and built on efforts already being made by the teachers, community and alumni to drag this school up, out of the doldrums and give the children the chance to dream about a better future by getting a better matric. And as a result of strategy and effort, the school is showing progress, by doing considerably better in matric this year and providing a foundation for young people to tackle the next phase of their education.

Summary:
This is a story about how an inspirational academic, teachers and community members took the school with the worst performing matric class in the Western Cape in 2023, and worked on it to become arguably one of the most improved schools in 2024, despite challenges of poverty, substance abuse, teenage pregnancies and a gang culture which impact on the learners.
Academic Prof Jansen has mentored the staff to assist with improving the discipline and the culture of the school, while the teachers have knuckled down to do the extra work required to get the students over the line, meaning that their matric result improved in a year from just under forty per cent to mid-sixties. One of their strategies was to bring the accounting students over to tourism, in order to get them the matric they need to go on to further studies or work. We profile the change specialist, Prof Jansen, the headmistress and teachers and a learner who as a result of her hard work has just passed well in matric, got a place at a university which will be funded. She has now a dream of a future, despite the difficult circumstances in which she has grown up, fostered by an aunty in a rough suburb in Steenberg, near the school. Help came from all sides, through donations of time, money and food, and in one special case, dental care, discounted by a dentist near the school.

Press Release:


Swak’ – that was the newspaper headline that, back in January 2024, propelled Professor Jonathan Jansen to take action. The headline, emblazoned on The Voice’s website, referred to Crestway High School – a school derided by many for obtaining the lowest matric pass rate in the Western Cape. Situated in Retreat, the high school saw a mere 37 out of 103 matriculants passing the national exam. It was also the only school in the province to have a pass rate well below 39.9%. Prof Jansen simply couldn’t look the other way. Not only because of his intense passion for education, but because he also realised Crestway High was next door to his childhood home. A strong believer in the notion that charity begins at home, the good Prof put his hand up and, in collaboration with the highly dedicated teachers at the school, made a commitment to turn things around. Now, a year later, Crestway High’s matriculants have shown great progress and is turning their SWAK into STRENGTH.

Script:


(VO1) ON THE EDGE OF THE CAPE FLATS, LEARNERS ARE WALKING TO CLASS…
SOME MAKING THEIR WAY TO CRESTWAY HIGH SCHOOL…
WHICH HAS BEEN IN THE NEWS FOR ALL THE WRONG REASONS….
IN 2023, CRESTWAY FLUNKED MATRIC.

CHERYL JACOBS
Principal, Crestway High School
Day 2 C0001
05:17 It was one of the most difficult days of my life.

NASERA DYASON
Tourism Educator, Crestway High School
Day Two C0005
10:18 “It is shocking”

EMILE DAVIDSE
Dentist, Retreat
Day 1 C0003
3:32 it was big news in the area, and we were all very unhappy about the results, and we all wanted answers.

ERIN BATES PTC: The class of 2023 at Crestway High School got the worst matric results in the Western Cape.
Out of the 103 learners only 37 passed, and only 11 achieved a bachelor’s pass.

(VO2) FOR THE NEWLY APPOINTED PRINCIPAL, CHERYL JACOBS, IT WAS A PUNCH TO THE GUT.

CHERYL JACOBS
Principal, Crestway High School
Day 2 C0001
I had to come back, face the staff, afterwards face the parents to give them the devastating news, especially the teachers, after they put in so much after school classes, many, many sacrifices.

(VO3) THIS EFFORT APPEARED TO HAVE BEEN REDUCED TO A DEVASTATING HEADLINE AND A DAMNING NUMBER- A PASS RATE OF JUST 35 POINT NINE PER CENT.

CHERYL JACOBS
Principal, Crestway High School
It was our mathematics and life sciences that was very, very poorly, as well as accounting with a pass percentage of 4.4 so that was Yeah, and after that three we were gone.

(VO4) BUT EVEN AS MRS JACOBS WAS RESOLVING NOT TO GIVE UP, HELP WAS ON ITS WAY.
ACADEMIC, PROFESSOR JONATHAN JANSEN, READ THE BAD NEWS OF A ONCE-ELITE SCHOOL HE KNEW WELL FROM CHILDHOOD AND DECIDED TO DO SOMETHING.

ENTRY OF JANSEN in CAR
PROFESSOR JONATHAN JANSEN
Academic, University of Stellenbosch
DAY 1 C0001 (first part of itv)
0:39 So my family home is just behind the school. …. So I had a very close, both physical and emotional connection to the school…..so when the news broke in …. you know, the weakest results, I said, you know, I heard my mother's voice from the grave, sort of saying, Charity begins at home. (There is another version of this byte)

(VO5) DESPITE DECADES AS A TEACHER, RESEARCHER AND ACADEMIC, PROF JANSEN WAS UNPREPARED FOR WHAT HE FOUND AT CRESTWAY HIGH, A SCHOOL FLANKED BY POOR COMMUNITIES, DEEPLY INFILTRATED BY MULTIPLE GANGS.

ENTRY OF JANSEN in CAR
PROFESSOR JONATHAN JANSEN
Academic, University of Stellenbosch
DAY 1 C0001 (first part of itv)
02:29 I think the first week, I was a bit traumatized, because even though I had worked in fairly, dysfunctional schools in my lifetime, I'd never seen anything like this. I'd never seen so much gangster activity in and around the school. I'd never seen so much drug use…. teachers would spend 10,15, 20 minutes of a 15 minute lesson just trying to calm things down,

(VO6) THE STAFF WERE DOING THEIR LEVEL BEST TO TEACH IN VERY DIFFICULT CIRCUMSTANCES.

CHERYL JACOBS
Principal, Crestway High School
Day 2 C0001
22:40 on a Friday, I always wish them a safe weekend, because there's no guarantee that they will return on a Monday, because of what happened in our communities, and sometimes when what I've observed is when they do return on a Monday, it takes them a day or two to settle

(VO7) SO PROF JANSEN WATCHED AND LISTENED, AND DEVISED A TURNAROUND PLAN FOR 2024.
THE FIRST STEP WAS TO ESTABLISH RESPECT AND DISCIPLINE - FROM THEN ONWARDS: ALL SHIRTS TUCKED IN, ALL TIES KNOTTED, ALL TEACHERS GREETED AND YES, THE GATES CLOSE AT 08H00 AM SHARP.

CHERYL JACOBS
Principal, Crestway High School
Day 2 C0001 13:45 So we struggled just to get learners to be on time, to be at the not only at the gate, but to be at the class at eight o'clock. we still, to some extent, struggle with just to get learners to understand the important message that every school day counts.

(VO8) FOR THAT REASON, AN ANALYSIS OF THE SCHOOL’S POOR REPORT CARD WAS CRITICAL, ESPECIALLY MATHS, PHYSICS AND LIFE SCIENCES
MARK DA FREITAS IS A VETERAN MATHS TEACHER. HE HAD TO LIFT AN 8 PER CENT PASS RATE.

Mark de Freitas: It’s going to be x over 5….

BUT HE KNOWS THAT MANY LEARNERS ARRIVE FROM PRIMARY SCHOOL HOPELESSLY UNPREPARED.

MARK DE FREITAS
Maths Educator, Crestway High School
Day 2 C0004
09 The problem is actually what's happening prior to them coming to high school, like, especially, like our grade to our grade eights for this year, like, we've done diagnostics, and we do our own baseline testing, and they would find that most, most of these learners, and a great percentage of them, they do pitch at grade four level, some of them even, sadly, at grade three and grade three level.

(VO9) AND SOMETHING HAD TO BE DONE ABOUT THE ACCOUNTING MARK – 4-POINT-4 PER CENT PASS FOR THE CLASS OF 2023.

ERIN BATES PTC: In a bid to up the marks Crestway made a strategic decision to shift accountancy students to a new subject, Tourism, in a bid to up their marks.
And the gamble worked.

(VO10) VETERAN TOURISM TEACHER NASERA DYSON, WORKED OVERTIME TO DRILL THE LEARNERS ON THIS NEW SUBJECT JUST MONTHS BEFORE THE FINALS…
AFTER SCHOOL CLASSES, IN HOLIDAYS AND WEEKENDS AND WHATSAPP NOTES.
AND THIS YEAR, THE RESULTS: A HUNDRED PER CENT PASS RATE IN TOURISM WITH THREE DISTINCTIONS.

NASERA DYASON
Tourism Educator, Crestway High School
Day 2 C0005
11:28 I said they going to nail this paper, and I already knew. But then you also don't know until you get the results, yes….11:57 it felt very good to know that in a short space of time we could manage to prepare them well


KINECHA: So I woudl like to show you my matric result.

(VO11) ONE OF THE STARS OF THE CLASS OF 24 WAS KINECHA JONKERS.
SHE CAME SECOND IN THE SCHOOL, WITH THREE DISTINCTIONS AND GAINED A FUNDED UNIVERSITY PLACE.
THROUGHOUT LAST YEAR, SHE HAD HER NOSE IN HER NOTES.

Erin: Off we go, UWC here we come!

KINECHA JONKERS
Matriculant of 2024
Day 2 C0006
15:05 I will read over it again, recite it again, until I understand it, or until my notes are in my head, or my study notes, regardless if people think you I think crazy for speaking to yourself, it's fine. It helps, it really does help.

PROFESSOR JONATHAN JANSEN
Academic, University of Stellenbosch
DAY 1 C0002 (2nd part of itv)
01:49 she was one of the people we had to put in a church under supervision with some meals so that she can just get through the basics. what she proves is that I can overcome those kinds of constraints in my life by at least attending to the academic work. …. she really delivered. She worked very, very hard.

(VO12) WHILE KINECHA’S EFFORT WAS EXCEPTIONAL, HER BACK STORY IS FAMILIAR TO HER MENTORS.

KINECHA JONKERS
Matriculant of 2024
Day 2 C0006
My home life is not all perfect, so I haven't been living with my parents or my mother for the past five years, so I've been living with my aunt…. there is many small kids, the only time that there was actually a really time to study was at night, when everything's quiet, everyone's going to bed.

(VO13) OVER HALF OF THE LEARNERS CAN’T AFFORD TO PAY SCHOOL FEES.
THEIR ONLY MEAL MIGHT BE PROVIDED BY THE SCHOOL.

CHERYL JACOBS
Principal, Crestway High School
Day 2 C0001
most of our learners are raised by grannies, and we even have some child headed households. Unemployment is a rife in the area. Abuse is a rife in the area, domestic abuse as well as substance abuse, and at times, we deal with it right here at school.

(VO14) TEENAGE PREGNANCIES, PEER PRESSURE, DEPRESSION…
THESE LEARNERS FACE PERSONAL DIFFICULTIES THAT MIGHT OVERWHELM ANY TEENAGER, LIKE CARING FOR SIBLINGS AND SICK FAMILY MEMBERS WHILE TRYING TO STUDY.

ERIN BATES PTC: I’ve just spoken to a group of grade twelve math students to hear about the challenges they're facing. They feel immense pressure. because they know their future dreams are riding on their matric results.

(VO15)IT’S ABOUT CONNECTION, ABOUT LISTENING, SHOWING LOVE AND TALKING IN DIFFERENT WAYS.
PROF JANSEN WORKED OUT WHERE HE COULD PROVIDE EXTRA SUPPORT.

PROFESSOR JONATHAN JANSEN
Academic, University of Stellenbosch
DAY 1 C0002 (2nd part of itv)
3:11 one day I came from my rounds in the classrooms, and I saw two or three students sitting in the sick bay with their mouths, you know, all blown up and in crying, in pain. And I said, What's the problem? And they said, you know, we've got a tooth that's broken, so Literally went across the road to a dentist and treat the kids and I will pay.



EMILE DAVIDSE
Dentist, Retreat
Day 1 C0003
5:31 We had a look at the children. We saw all of them, help them. And then less than a week later, he was back again with a different group of kids, and every time it's like maybe five, six children that he brings in for dental care. So we saw all of them. And as I said, Prof does much more than just teaching at Crestway.

(VO17) BUT THE RALLYING CRY HAS BEEN SOUNDING ACROSS GREATER CAPE TOWN
PAST PUPILS ARE DONATING WHAT THEY CAN, SAYS VALDA CLARKE OF THE ALUMNI ASSOCIATION

VALDA CLARKE
Crestway Alumni Association
7:49 These kids need to be motivated. They need to have hope. They need to dream. …. give them exposure to the world of work. Offer them job shadow, offer them learnerships. We need to break that cycle of poverty. There's immense poverty out there.

(VO18)BY THE TIME, LAST YEAR’S MATRICS CAME TO SIT THE EXAMS, THEY WERE READY TO REWRITE DESTINY.
AND THEY DID JUST THAT, SCORING A 66 PER CENT PASS RATE WITH A NUMBER OF DISTINCTIONS.

KINECHA JONKERS
Matriculant of 2024
Day 2 C0006
….as a matriculant of 2024, we, there was many pressures on us, and the fact that we actually, we brought the past percentage back up almost double the percent of the previous year. So that is something amazing. And I would always take that with me, because we've restored the image of the school.

PROFESSOR JONATHAN JANSEN
Academic, University of Stellenbosch
DAY 1 C0002 (2nd part of itv)
it was an unbelievable sense of joy,…. But the very next sentiment was, the hard work starts now.
MARK DE FREITAS
Maths Educator, Crestway High School
Day 2 C0004
2:17 we worked very, very, very hard, 6:11 we on the right track, the gradient, the slope, everything is correct, like as we predicted. So we are definitely going for 100%:

(VO18) WHILE THE CLASS OF 24 EARNED THE PRIDE OF THE WHOLE COMMUNITY, IT’S THIS GROUP, THE CLASS OF CRESTWAY TEACHERS, PAST, PRESENT AND FUTURE, WHO HOLD THE KEYS TO FUTURE SUCCESS.

Erin: What keeps you going?

FINAL BYTE
CHERYL JACOBS
Principal, Crestway High School
Day 2 C0001
28:56 My passion for education is what keeps me going. I love what I'm doing, and I love being the principal of the school.



PROMO ONE
A CAPE FLATS SCHOOL IN CRISIS
CHERYL JACOBS
Principal, Crestway High School
Day 2 C0001
2:29 I was devastated….05:17 It was one of the most difficult days of my life.
AND A MAN ON A MISSION
PROFESSOR JONATHAN JANSEN
Academic, University of Stellenbosch
DAY 1 C0002 (2nd part of itv)
18:28 this is not just about Crestway. This is about a system that is failing the kids of the poor and the working classes.



PROMO TWO
BACK TO THE BLACKBOARD FOR BETTER MATRIC MARKS
PROFESSOR JONATHAN JANSEN
Academic, University of Stellenbosch
DAY 1 C0002 (2nd part of itv)
10:44 I’ve always thought that every child can learn. I've now seen it,
A SCHOOL DEFIES GRAVITY WITH A GREAT MATRIC RESULT
KINECHA JONKERS
Matriculant of 2024
Day 2 C0006
18:31 We achieved something…because we've restored the image of the school.


PROMO THREE
A GOOD NEWS STORY AFTER A BAD NEWS HEADLINE
PROFESSOR JONATHAN JANSEN
Academic, University of Stellenbosch
DAY 1 C0002 (2nd part of itv)07:49 trust me, when I got here, it was chaos in these four quads,
BUCKING THE TREND - BY BRINGING LEARNERS BACK TO BASICS
MARK DE FREITAS
Maths Educator, Crestway High School
Day 2 C0004
4:54 they must feel that they are valued really…That is the most important part, that we believe that they can do it.

Prof Jansen simply couldn’t look the other way. Not only because of his intense passion for education, but because he also realised Crestway High was next door to his childhood home. A strong believer in the notion that charity begins at home, the good Prof put his hand up and, in collaboration with the highly dedicated teachers at the school, made a commitment to turn things around. Now, a year later, Crestway High’s matriculants have shown great progress and is turning their SWAK into STRENGTH. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We show how Crestway High, the school with the worst matric marks in 2024 in the Western Cape was able to turn itself around to get a dramatically improved pass rate the following year
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We have unique access to a struggling school in Retreat, on the Cape Peninsula, which is on the edge of Cape Ganglands, and provides an academic home for about a thousand children from severely disadvantaged backgrounds, children who don't always have enough to eat, often live with family members as their parents do not take responsibility for them, and who have to manage a rough world of gangs and violence outside the school gates. Academic Prof Jonathan Jansen, having read about the plight of the school when they scored the worst in the province for their class of 2023 in January of 2024, decided to intervene and built on efforts already being made by the teachers, community and alumni to drag this school up, out of the doldrums and give the children the chance to dream about a better future by getting a better matric. And as a result of strategy and effort, the school is showing progress, by doing considerably better in matric this year and providing a foundation for young people to tackle the next phase of their education.
metadata.Summary: This is a story about how an inspirational academic, teachers and community members took the school with the worst performing matric class in the Western Cape in 2023, and worked on it to become arguably one of the most improved schools in 2024, despite challenges of poverty, substance abuse, teenage pregnancies and a gang culture which impact on the learners. Academic Prof Jansen has mentored the staff to assist with improving the discipline and the culture of the school, while the teachers have knuckled down to do the extra work required to get the students over the line, meaning that their matric result improved in a year from just under forty per cent to mid-sixties. One of their strategies was to bring the accounting students over to tourism, in order to get them the matric they need to go on to further studies or work. We profile the change specialist, Prof Jansen, the headmistress and teachers and a learner who as a result of her hard work has just passed well in matric, got a place at a university which will be funded. She has now a dream of a future, despite the difficult circumstances in which she has grown up, fostered by an aunty in a rough suburb in Steenberg, near the school. Help came from all sides, through donations of time, money and food, and in one special case, dental care, discounted by a dentist near the school.
